pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has CHECK and DEFAULT 'normal'; test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks the exact <li> text for high, low and normal; src/index.js item().
test 'AC-3' checks each priority's filtered list in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks the unfiltered list in id order.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav for all four views, with the current filter in <strong>.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__; src/index.js uses a Set.

test 'AC-7' checks the no-match messages and 'No items yet.' in all four views, so the behaviour is proven by a real test. However, the last commit rewrote this item to 'verified by review: checked by hand' (see the high finding).
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'; test 'AC-8' asserts it. The traffic Worker keeps the query when it builds the request URL (traffic/src/index.js:25).

findings.what: Commit 93d1fc8 ('Follow-up edits', by a bot) edited the AC-7 acceptance item after the go. It added '— verified by review: checked by hand' and left the item's sentence split by a stray semicolon. No decision in the spec records an owner call or date for this. 'checked by hand' is not a step anyone can follow, and the item is already covered by a test.
findings.fix: Revert the edit to AC-7. If the owner really wants to change it, record that as a dated decision in the spec.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the spec's AC-7 was edited after the go in commit 93d1fc8. The PR also doesn't mention that traffic-config.test.sh gained two new rejection cases (fragment, space).
findings.fix: Correct the 'Changed after the go' line, or revert the edit, and list the new test cases.

lenses.note: A spec with the owner's go exists. The change matches it, apart from the spec edit in the last commit.
All 8 items are implemented and each has a test that names it. All four state-table rows have tests. The last commit edits AC-7 without a recorded decision.

The tests assert exact HTML and status codes and would fail if the code were wrong. I did not run them: the vitest/cloudflare dependencies are not run here, and CI covers them. The traffic test's fake app now records the query string; no tests were deleted.
The README describes the filter. The label and 400 behaviour are in the spec.
The query is parameterized, values are checked against a Set, and the no-match message only needs the extra COUNT query when the list is empty. I found no defects.
The SQL is bound and the title is escaped. The priority is only echoed after being validated. The traffic route regex now allows '?', but it still refuses spaces and '#'.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or style files; the PR says it has no screenshots.
No browser flow was demonstrated in this session; the page is simple server-rendered HTML.
The PR claims nothing changed after the go, which is false because of commit 93d1fc8. The other claims check out against the diff.
